messages:
marta: Quick RFC follow-up — proposal to extract session-store + minimal request-surface into a dedicated 'session-store' service. Keeps hotpath thin, allows per-tenant scaling for large stateful customers. Short notes below.

marta: Goals: 1) Isolate session KV caching and eviction policy; 2) Remove runtime dependency between router and enrichment layer; 3) Enable independent deploy cadence & autoscale.

marta: Minimal API sketch:
```http
POST /v1/session/get
{ "session_id": "...", "keys": ["kv1","kv2"] }

POST /v1/session/patch
{ "session_id":"...", "ops": [...] }
```

sam: How do we keep latency under 10ms for hot reads? network hop adds cost. Can we co-locate with runtime or use sidecar caching?

marta: Good point. Plan: colocate in same AZ, optional in-process LRU sidecar for sub-1ms cold-start, and a small KV prefix-cache at router for last-token cache. We'll also support a best-effort sticky routing to reduce cross-node hops.

jules: About migration: recommend adapter shim in router that can forward to new service with fallback to in-process store. Canary by tenant (10% traffic) first. Observability: gRPC + per-tenant latency & miss rate metrics.

leo: Need clear ownership of GC/compaction. Previously we had multiple services tinkering with eviction — that caused incidents. Suggest single GC owner in session-store with configurable per-tenant policy; roll out with read-only mode for 1 week before full cutover.

arch-bot: RFC-312 linked: https://internal.redwood/rfcs/312-session-store-extract — includes perf numbers, cost delta, and rollout playbook.

marta: Next steps: I'll draft a narrow PR for the adapter shim + interface contract. @sam @jules @leo please review perf targets and compaction policy by EOD Friday. If OK we'll book a 30m deep-dive Monday.

sam: ACK, will add perf test harness.

jules: I'll add dashboard panels and alert thresholds.

leo: I'll prepare a runbook for GC and rollback.

marta: Thanks — will ping calendar invite.
